answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may post bids, with one bid per locked token in each auction. The lock does not prove a person is behind the agent; it makes influence costly to multiply. An attacker creating thousands of identities must buy and immobilize thousands of tokens, paying opportunity cost and risking slashing for fraud. A quill account cannot gain weight from an onyx name alone: each claim must stand on the same collateral ledge.
